etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English restreynte, from Old French restreinte; more at restrain.

definitions.definition: (countable) something that restrains, ties, fastens or secures

quote.citation: November 2 2014, Daniel Taylor, “Sergio Agüero strike wins derby for Manchester City against 10-man United”, in guardian.co.uk:
quote.text: City will feel nonplussed when they review the tape and Pellegrini had to summon all his restraint in the post-match interviews.
